title: A marketplace refund route can separate prior direct correction from later public redress
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission GOAT enforcement and refund-administration pages
geography: United States consumers using GOAT online marketplace

observations.period: 2025 direct refund stage and October 6, 2026 FTC distribution

denominator.unit: customers receiving FTC checks or PayPal payments in October 2026; aggregate recipient count

prior_direct_refunds.unit: more than U.S. dollars returned by GOAT to affected customers in 2025

current_ftc_distribution.unit: more than U.S. dollars in checks and PayPal payments sent by FTC in October 2026

payment_channels.value: Most recipients receive a mailed check; some receive PayPal

payment_window.value: Checks should be cashed within 90 days; PayPal payments should be redeemed within 30 days

underlying_control_issue.value: FTC alleged late priority-processing shipments, failure to offer prompt cancellation/refund options, and failure to consistently honor Buyer Protection refunds

observations.method: Structured extraction from official FTC GOAT refund and press-release pages; direct company refunds, FTC distribution, payment channel, and acceptance window remain separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The public pages do not disclose the full eligible denominator, individual amount, delivery, check cashing, PayPal redemption, returned payment, residual product or shipping loss, repeat use, trust, switching, or exit.
observations.subgroup: GOAT customers affected by expedited-shipping delays or deficient-product/refund issues who did not previously receive a company refund; the October 2026 count is not a complete historical harm denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: A second public distribution may improve reach after direct refunds, while short cashing or redemption windows can leave usable receipt dependent on address, payment access, attention, or administrative effort.

related_sources.claim: The FTC describes the October 2026 distribution, prior GOAT refunds, alleged shipping/refund failures, administrator, and payment windows.
The FTC case page identifies the GOAT enforcement matter and court-order context.

boundary: This record establishes a named marketplace control failure, prior direct refunds, and a later FTC-administered distribution with defined payment windows. It does not establish individual receipt, adequacy, product correction, continued use, switching, trust repair, or durable household recovery.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official FTC refund page HTML retrieved through the search.ftc.gov mirror for extraction
